Running sims now — summary notes inline. I've attached the CSV outputs in the sheet. Highlights:

- Baseline model: open-llm-7B quantized to int8 (our verified profile).
- Tokens per chat response (median / p95): 180 / 420 tokens (these are for the sample prompts; we'll compute over their eval set).
- Cache sensitivity (prefix/KV):
  * 0% hit -> avg tokens generated = 420 (no saved prefix)
  * 50% hit -> avg tokens generated = 300
  * 90% hit -> avg tokens generated = 210
- Unit cost (hosting tier assumptions in sheet):
  * Hosted default (no reserved): ~$3.40 per 100k output tokens @ int8 kernels
  * Dedicated reserved (committed): ~$2.05 per 100k output tokens @ int8 kernels
- Batching impact (sampled):
  * Per-request (no batching): baseline latency per token = 1.2ms, throughput low, cost identical per-token but higher infra overhead.
  * Pooled batching (50ms batch window): improves throughput by 1.6x, reduces per-token cost by ~22%, increases tail latency risk (p95 token latency moves from 1.2ms to 3.0ms in worst-case burst) — but with Redwood's dynamic routing we can keep API-level p95 under 400ms for chat responses by routing urgent requests to low-latency pool.
- Quantization notes: int4 reduces per-token cost by additional ~18% in dedicated pools but may increase generation time by ~5-12% on some ops and can slightly change tokenization behavior (edge-case prompts). Recommend int8 for pilot; consider int4 for steady-state after eval.

I'll attach a small sensitivity table here in the sheet and tag the rows used for the MAP gating thresholds.

Karthik
